## Problem statement

The refactor skill filed an `E741` ("ambiguous variable name: `l`") finding at
line 4756 of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
and injected a `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker. Investigation shows the
finding is a **false positive**: no committed revision of the file has ever
contained an `l` identifier, and `ruff check` on the current file passes.

## Users

- **Maintainers of the proxy-usage-analysis skill** — need a worklog that does
  not carry phantom technical debt.
- **The refactor skill / future lint sweeps** — need accurate detection; stale
  markers suppress future findings for the same smell type in this file.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the worklog to reflect real defects so triage time is
  not spent re-verifying already-clean code.
- As an agent running `/skill:refactor`, I want a stale `REFACTOR` marker to be
  removed once its smell no longer exists, so the marker does not mask new
  findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --select E741 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports no findings.
- [ ] An AST scan (or equivalent) confirms no `Name`/`arg` identifier equal to `l` (or the other E741 names `O`/`I`) exists in the file.
- [ ] The work item's disposition is recorded in a comment: either **closed as resolved-in-parent** (smell fixed before parent commit `c0f3625f`, no code change) or the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block is removed from the file.
- [ ] Testing/validation criterion: the verification commands above are documented in the work item so a reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The finding references a **deleted worktree path**
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4-surface-attribution-in-reporting-py/`);
  the authoritative file is the main checkout copy.
- `AGENTS.md` repository boundaries: `.pi/` must not be edited unless
  explicitly instructed — removing the marker requires explicit authorisation.
- The repo already carries other stale `REFACTOR` markers (e.g.
  `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` in the same file, `LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`,
  `LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`); a one-off removal would be inconsistent without the
  systemic fix.

## Existing state

- Current HEAD file: 5,023 lines; line 4756 is the docstring
  `"""LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4 — attribution surfaces in the report."""` — a docstring,
  not a variable.
- Every committed revision (40 commits touching the file) checked: zero
  standalone `l` identifiers. `git log -S "for l in"` returns nothing.
- `ruff check` on the file: **All checks passed!**
- AST scan for `Name`/`arg` in `{l, O, I}`: **NONE**.
- The parent item `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` ("Surface attribution in reporting.py")
  is `completed`/`done`; its commit `c0f3625f` is the one that both injected the
  marker and (evidently) landed the fixed file — so the smell was resolved in
  the same session, before commit.

## Desired change

Minimal: record the false-positive/resolved-in-parent disposition and close the
item. Optional (requires explicit authorisation under the `.pi/` boundary
rule): delete the six-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block so the
`formatting` smell type is no longer suppressed for this file.

Systemic follow-up (out of scope, filed as `discovered-from`): the refactor
skill should remove a `REFACTOR` marker when its work item is closed — it
currently only injects (`comment_injection.py` has no removal path), so stale
markers accumulate repo-wide.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — lines 1–6 hold the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block (optional removal).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixtures used by the file; no change expected.
- `.ruff.toml` — confirms `E` (incl. `E741`) is selected and not ignored; no change expected.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` — Surface attribution in reporting.py (parent session that injected the marker; completed).
- `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` — Refactor: unused variable `schedule`, same file/marker mechanism (completed; marker still present).
- `LP-0MU1I7T37001CV4O` — ruff I001 candidate false positive at another file (closed as duplicate of an already-fixed parent finding; disposition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `l` variable existed only in the pre-commit worktree state

- **Risk (scope creep):** "also clean up every stale REFACTOR marker" — record

- **Risk:** removing the marker alone does not fix the systemic leak; without

- **Risk:** misclassifying a real finding as false positive. Mitigated by the

- Q: "Is this E741 finding real, or a false positive?" — Answer (Map, evidence-based): **False positive.** No committed revision contains an `l` identifier; `ruff check` passes; AST scan finds no `l`/`O`/`I` names. - Q: "Should the stale `REFACTOR` marker be removed as part of this item?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION for the producer.** Recommended: close as resolved-in-parent without touching `.pi/` (respects the repository-boundaries rule); file a separate `discovered-from` item for the systemic marker-removal gap. # Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`

# Measure slot save cost: wall time, on-disk size, success rate

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 1 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A measured table of `slot save` cost for prompt sizes 38K / 72K / 100K / 124K
tokens: wall-clock time, on-disk snapshot size, bytes per token, and success
rate — including the intermittent ReadTimeout failures, which must be counted,
not retried away.

## Minimal implementation

- Measurement mode in `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
  (`--mode save --sizes 38000,72000,100000,124000 --reps N`).
- Per repetition: unique salted prompt → completion to force a real prefill into
  the slot → `POST /slots/{id}?action=save` → record elapsed, status, on-disk
  `stat().st_size` of the snapshot, plus the llama-server log's own
  `prompt_save: - saving prompt with length N, total state size = X MiB` line for
  cross-validation.
- Derive bytes/token = size / prompt_n and compare with the profile's physical
  KV-per-token expectation from `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py`.
- Emit `results/<label>/save.json` + a markdown table with per-size
  p50 / p90 / max save seconds and success rate; failures broken out by
  outcome class (`timeout`, `http_error`, `exception`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Results table covering all four prompt sizes with, per size: n attempts,
  success rate, save wall time p50/p90/max, snapshot size, bytes/token.
- Observed failure rate and failure classes recorded explicitly; if zero failures
  occur the report states the sample size and the window's historical rate
  (`slot_save failed` count) instead of implying saves are reliable.
- The llama-server log's `total state size` agrees with the on-disk size within
  5%, or the discrepancy is reported with an explanation.
- Repeated runs are reproducible: re-running with the same `--sizes`/`--reps`
  produces a new timestamped result directory and does not overwrite prior
  results.
- The run is safe to interrupt and leaves no snapshot it did not record
  (cleanup of its own files listed in the results).

## Constraints

- Save must be issued only when the slot is otherwise idle; concurrent saves are
  serialised by llama-server and would inflate the timing.
- Snapshot files are large (~0.5-0.7 GiB each) — the run must cap total bytes
  written and clean up after itself via `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
  semantics, without touching snapshots it did not create.

## Risks

- The `session_slot_skip_when_busy` production gate does not exist in this
  harness path, so saves will be issued under whatever load exists; the run must
  record competing local activity (proxy `local_dispatch_records`) per attempt.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/save.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
- `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md` (evidence schema reference)

# Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (the core spike question)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 2 — this is the load-bearing question:
does a restore actually avoid re-prefill, and how much does it cost?

## Target outcome

For each prompt size (38K / 72K / 100K / 124K), a paired comparison between
(a) a **cold** run — fresh slot, no snapshot, full prefill — and (b) a
**restored** run — save, evict/clear the slot, restore, then replay the same
prompt — reporting time-to-first-token, tokens actually evaluated
(`timings.prompt_n`), tokens reused from cache, and the resulting hit-rate.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode restore` in the harness: for each size and repetition run the pair
  `cold` then `save → clear slot → restore → replay` and record both rows.
- Hit is derived from tokens, not wall time: `cached_tokens = prompt_total -
  timings.prompt_n`, `cached_ratio = cached_tokens / prompt_total`. A run is a
  **hit** when `cached_ratio >= --hit-threshold` (default 0.9); a run is a
  **miss** when the restore returned OK but `prompt_n` shows a full re-prefill.
  Latency is reported alongside, never used as the primary hit definition.
- Report per size: cold prefill seconds (p50), restored first-byte seconds (p50),
  speed-up factor, hit-rate, and miss/partial-hit distribution.
- Cross-check against the llama-server log (restored-checkpoint lines / full
  re-processing markers) and against `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
  from the completion response, recording any disagreement.
- `results/<label>/restore.json` + markdown table; the JSON must be directly
  consumable by the break-even model in the verdict child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paired cold-vs-restored table for all four sizes, n >= 3 per cell, with
  per-size: cold TTFT p50, restored TTFT p50, speed-up, hit-rate, and the
  distribution of `cached_ratio`.
- The hit definition (`cached_ratio >= threshold`) is documented in the results
  output and the doc, and both the token-based and latency-based views are
  reported so the verdict can cite either.
- Partial hits are reported distinctly from full misses (a 40% prefix reuse is
  not a "miss").
- Any disagreement between `timings.prompt_n`, the response
  `cached_tokens`, and the llama-server log markers is reported, not silently
  reconciled.
- The cold baseline for each size is measured in the same run and window as its
  restored pair, so no cross-run drift is attributed to restore.
- Results are reproducible (timestamped result dir; salt recorded so the same
  prompts can be regenerated).

## Constraints

- The restore must be issued into a slot that does not already hold the same
  prefix, otherwise the measurement proves nothing — the harness must clear or
  overwrite the slot between save and restore and assert that it did.

## Risks

- If llama-server refuses to restore a snapshot for a hybrid-attention model, the
  failure will surface as either an explicit non-200 or a silent full re-prefill.
  The harness must distinguish these (this is the difference between "restore is
  broken" and "restore is ignored").

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/restore.json` (new artifact)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (`_restore_slot_snapshot` semantics)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` (cached-token derivation reference)
data.title: Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (cold vs restored, paired)

# Characterise restored-cache invalidation (hybrid-attention behaviour)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 3.

## Target outcome

Quantified answer to the hypothesis risk in the parent: this build is Qwen3.x
hybrid attention + recurrent/SWA, and llama.cpp already invalidates its own
context checkpoints, so a restored snapshot may be rejected or only partially
usable. Produce a measured invalidation rate by *reuse shape*, plus the tokens
re-processed as a result.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode invalidation` in the harness, driving four restore shapes per size:
  1. exact replay — same prompt, no extension (best case);
  2. one-turn extension — same prompt + a short follow-up user turn (the real
     session pattern);
  3. prefix drift — same prompt with a modified system-prompt head (should
     always miss, guards against over-crediting);
  4. cold control — no snapshot at all.
- Parse llama-server log markers between requests: `forcing full prompt
  re-processing`, `erased invalidated context checkpoint ... n_swa`,
  `restored context checkpoint`, and `n_past = ... slot.prompt.tokens.size()`.
  Attribute markers to an attempt by slot id + log offset captured immediately
  before and after each request.
- Report per shape: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, mean/median tokens
  re-processed, and the effective usable prefix (cached tokens on the first
  completion after restore).
- Emit `results/<label>/invalidation.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invalidation table for the four restore shapes at each prompt size, with
  n >= 3 per cell: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, tokens re-processed
  (median/p90), effective usable prefix fraction.
- Requirement from `AGENTS.md` respected: `forcing full prompt re-processing` is
  reported as *expected hybrid-arch behaviour with a cost*, never as a defect —
  the table quantifies the cost, and the doc says so explicitly.
- The prefix-drift control behaves as expected (near-zero usable prefix); if it
  does not, the recording/attribution method is reported as unproven and the
  numbers are marked non-authoritative rather than published as fact.
- The one-turn-extension shape is measured, because it is the shape that decides
  whether virtual slots help real sessions (which always extend context).
- Log-marker attribution method is documented so another operator can reproduce
  the counts from the raw logs.

## Constraints

- llama-server logs carry no timestamps — attribution must use log byte offsets
  captured around each request, per the caveat in
  `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md`.
- Read-only access to `/var/log/llama-proxy/`; no log rewriting.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` (log-parsing reference)
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (window-metric reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/invalidation.json` (new artifact)

# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.
- No `drop_caches` unless explicitly permitted by the operator; measure the
  natural page-cache behaviour instead.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/memory.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`

# Harness-side virtual-slot prototype: 8 session slots over 2 physical slots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 5 — the end-to-end contention
comparison. **Gated on OPEN QUESTION 2** (recorded on the parent): AC5 of the
spike asks for 8 virtual slots over 2 physical slots, but virtual slots do not
exist and must not be added to production. This child delivers the measurement
as a *harness-side prototype* unless the producer directs otherwise.

## Target outcome

A measured p50/p90 first-byte latency and throughput comparison between
(A) 2 logical sessions on 2 physical slots (today's baseline) and (B) 8 logical
sessions multiplexed onto 2 physical slots by swap-in/swap-out of KV snapshots,
using a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload.

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/benchmarks/virtual_slot_prototype.py` (or a `--mode virtual` in the
  harness): an 8-entry session table mapping logical session → physical
  llama-server slot; on dispatch it restores the session's snapshot into a free
  physical slot (evicting the current occupant with a save first), issues the
  completion, then saves the session's snapshot back.
- Workload: 8 concurrent synthetic sessions, each doing K turns with a shared
  prefix and per-turn growth, sized from the spike's four prompt sizes; turn
  gaps chosen to force real evictions.
- Metrics per configuration: TTFT p50/p90, per-session abandon count (requests
  that could not get a physical slot within the configured queue budget — the
  harness's analogue of `fallback_after_queue`), save/restore counts and
  failures, restored-hit rate, and completion count.
- Both configurations run back-to-back in one invocation so drift is shared.
- Emit `results/<label>/contention.json` + markdown table with an explicit
  A/B delta column.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A/B table for N_logical = 2 (baseline) vs N_logical = 8 over 2 physical slots:
  TTFT p50/p90, throughput, abandon count, save/restore counts, hit-rate,
  per-configuration duration.
- The eviction cost is counted, not hidden: for every restore that displaces
  another session, the displaced session's next-turn cold cost is measured and
  reported (this is the "eviction cost it imposes" term the parent requires).
- The run states plainly whether the prototype is a faithful model of a
  production virtual-slot implementation, listing the differences (no proxy
  routing, no dispatch leases, no contention queue) — no implied production
  parity.
- If 8-over-2 cannot complete within a bounded budget (e.g. wall-clock cap), the
  partial result is reported with the completion fraction rather than being
  silently truncated.
- The prototype lives only under `proxy/benchmarks/`; a test/documentation
  assertion confirms no production module is imported for dispatch.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change (parent AC5).
- Must not starve live sessions: the run requires a quiet window or an explicit
  recorded validity caveat, mirroring
  `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` § `Fidelity caveats`.

## Risks

- Two prior live sweeps failed under concurrent load (600-760 s stalls,
  llama-server health probes unanswered). If the quiet window cannot be obtained,
  this child must fall back to the analytic model in the verdict child and say
  so — do not retry the live run indefinitely.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (concurrency/sweep reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_simulation.py` (queue-model reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/contention.json` (new artifact)

# Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Satisfies AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A committed document `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` containing
the complete measured tables, an explicit break-even inequality, a go/no-go
verdict, and — if not viable — the cheaper substitutes ranked with the measured
evidence for each.

## Minimal implementation

# Intake brief — slot_benchmark: record finish_reason per request

**Headline:** Record each benchmark request's `finish_reason` in `slot_<N>.json`, aggregate it into `summary.finish_reason_counts` (with an explicit missing-reason count) and surface the `length` count in the human-readable summary plus the per-slot console summary, so the N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep can report the required `finish_reason=length` metric instead of "not recorded".

## Problem statement

The slot-count sweep's acceptance criteria require a `finish_reason=length` count (a smaller per-slot context at N=3/N=4 is expected to truncate more responses), but `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` records no completion reason per request — a `slot_<N>.json` request row carries only `request_index/status/total_duration_seconds/time_to_first_token_seconds/prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/tokens_per_second/resolved_model/error`. The value cannot be recovered post hoc either, because `restart_services()` truncates `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` during the restore restart, so the 2026-10-23 sweep had to record the metric as **not recorded**.

## Users

- **Producer / capacity owner** deciding `session_slot_pool_size` (keep N=2 vs move to N=3/N=4): needs the truncation count next to TTFT/decode/queue metrics to judge the per-slot-context trade-off.
  - *As a capacity owner, I want the number of truncated (`finish_reason=length`) responses per slot count so I can weigh added decode concurrency against smaller per-slot context.*
- **Benchmark operator** re-running the sweep: wants the metric in the artefacts already produced by the run, with no extra log-parsing step and no dependence on proxy logs surviving the run.
  - *As the operator, I want `summary.finish_reason_counts` in `slot_<N>.json` so the sweep evidence table can be filled in from committed artefacts alone.*

## Existing state

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py:1045` `send_request()` posts a **non-streaming** chat completion (`"stream": False`, line ~1071) and builds `RequestResult` from `usage` + `X-Resolved-Model`; the response body's `choices[0].finish_reason` is read nowhere.
- `RequestResult` (line ~541) and `SlotRunResult.summary()` (line ~603) are the two places that shape `slot_<N>.json` request rows and the per-run summary.
- `generate_report()` (line ~1414) writes `slot_benchmark_report.json` + `slot_benchmark_summary.txt`; `main()` (line ~1964) prints a per-slot inline summary.
- An in-repo precedent for the exact key name and rendering exists: `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` builds `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` from `Stream finished: … reason=<x>` log lines and renders "Stream finish reasons: …".
- The gap is already documented and linked: `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` lines 232, 289–290, 365 record `finish_reason=length` as "not recorded (harness gap, LP-0MVLHNJ3W007T319)".
- Tests live in `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` (report/aggregation/CLI only; no test covers `send_request`).

## Desired change

1. Capture the reason per request in `send_request()` from the non-streaming body (`data["choices"][0].get("finish_reason")`), store it on `RequestResult` as `finish_reason: str | None` (**appended last**, so existing positional constructions stay valid), and emit it in `to_dict()`.
2. Aggregate in `SlotRunResult.summary()`: `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` over completed requests, plus an explicit count of completed requests that reported no reason (absent/nullable reason reported rather than silently omitted, matching the `contention.unavailable` convention already used in this module).
3. Render it: a dedicated finish-reason block in `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` (per slot count: each reason's count, the `length` count, and the missing count) and the same information in the per-slot inline console summary. The existing main table columns stay unchanged.
4. Document the new per-request key and summary field in `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` with a `python -c` inspection snippet (mirroring the existing contention-metrics section).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `slot_<N>.json` request row carries `finish_reason`, taken from the non-streaming response body's `choices[0].finish_reason`, and `null` when the request errored (non-200/exception) or the provider returned no reason — verified by unit tests that stub the HTTP response.
2. `summary.finish_reason_counts` (present in `slot_<N>.json`, in `slot_benchmark_report.json` `runs[].summary`, and in the in-memory `SlotRunResult.summary()`) maps each observed reason to its count over completed requests, so a truncation count is readable directly as `summary.finish_reason_counts["length"]`, and completed requests with no recorded reason are counted explicitly (not dropped).
3. `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` contains a finish-reason section reporting, per slot count, each reason's count including `length` and the missing-reason count (with `--`/explicit wording when no run recorded any), and the per-slot inline console summary prints the same finish-reason line — both asserted by tests reading the generated artefacts.
4. `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documents the new per-request `finish_reason` key, the `summary.finish_reason_counts` field and the missing-reason count, including a runnable `python -c` snippet that prints the per-slot reason counts from `slot_benchmark_report.json`.
5. `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` gains tests covering: `send_request` capture of a present reason, a missing/null reason (counted as missing), an error request (`finish_reason` is `null`), mixed-reason aggregation in `summary()`, and the summary-file/console rendering — and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No streaming capture path is required.** The harness only issues non-streaming requests (`stream: False`); the streaming variant named in the seed description does not exist in this file. Adding a streaming mode is out of scope (see Assumptions).
- **Backwards compatibility of the artefacts and dataclass:** `RequestResult` is constructed positionally in existing tests and `summary` keys are consumed by `compare_results.py`-style delta comparisons — append the new field last with a default and do not rename/remove existing summary keys or main-table columns.
- **No new production instrumentation, no proxy changes** — the metric comes from the benchmark's own HTTP responses.
- **Do not backfill historical runs.** `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/` cannot be repaired (the restore restart cleared the proxy log); `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` is a historical record and stays as-is (it already links this item as the gap).
- Marker for "no reason recorded" must be distinguishable from reason `"stop"`/`"length"` — do not conflate absent with a fabricated default.
- Restyling/renumbering the existing human-readable report sections is out of scope (only additive changes plus the one console line).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — non-streaming only:** `send_request()` fixes `stream: False`; the non-streaming `choices[0].finish_reason` is the correct capture point. If a streaming harness is added later, a follow-up item must extend the capture to the last streamed chunk.
- **Assumption — key naming:** `finish_reason_counts` is reused verbatim from `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` so slot evidence tables and extract reports read consistently.
- **Assumption — absence is reported, not guessed:** completed requests with no `finish_reason` are counted separately; the sweep reading rule (only meaningful for locally served requests) is documented rather than enforced.
- **Risk — misleading `length` counts under remote fallback:** a remote provider may report `stop` for a response the local slot would have truncated, so `finish_reason_counts` must be read together with the existing `contention.local_stream_share` (and per-request `resolved_model`). *Mitigation:* AC4 documentation states this reading rule; no per-provider cross-tab is added (scope control).
- **Risk — artefact consumers:** a renamed/removed summary key or a widened main table could break delta comparisons in existing result notes. *Mitigation:* additive-only change (new field appended, new section, existing columns untouched).
- **Risk — scope creep:** per-provider `length` cross-tabs, streaming capture, historical backfill and a proxy-side `finish_reason` metric are all plausible follow-ons. *Mitigation:* they are explicitly out of scope here and should be recorded as linked items if wanted, not folded in.
- **Risk — the metric alone does not unblock the sweep:** the 2026-10-23 runs were also INVALID on local concurrency (`LP-0MVLHNEDO008FTBH`), so this item removes one blocker but does not by itself make the sweep decision-ready.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — Needs `RequestResult.finish_reason` (+`to_dict`), capture in `send_request()`, `finish_reason_counts` + missing count in `SlotRunResult.summary()`, a finish-reason section in `generate_report()`, and one extra line in the per-slot inline summary in `main()`.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — Needs new tests for capture (stubbed `httpx` response), absence/error handling, aggregation and rendering.
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` — Needs documentation of the new per-request key, summary field, reading rule (pair with `local_stream_share`) and an inspection snippet.
- `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` — No change expected; reference implementation for the `finish_reason_counts` naming/rendering convention.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVK09622002CRMR` — Record slot-count verdict and reconcile with projection (discovered-from; its AC1 evidence table requires the `finish_reason=length` count).
- `LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD` — Run controlled N=3/N=4 slot-count sweep in a quiet window (parent epic of the predecessor).
- `LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH` — Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window (the run that recorded the metric as "not recorded").
- `LP-0MVLHNEDO008FTBH` — Slot-sweep harness cannot exercise local concurrency: add a warm-start / staggered-arrival mode (parallel harness gap; listed as a precondition alongside this item).
- `LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` — Re-evaluate `session_slot_pool_size` against measured GPU busy-time and contention history (defines the metric set; its doc records this gap).
- `LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC` — prefill-aware busy metrics (sibling metric gap for the same sweep).
- `LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD` — Slot-count benchmark: find optimal `session_slot_pool_size` for Qwen3 (original harness item).
- `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` + `tests/test_slot_history_extract.py` — existing `finish_reason_counts` implementation to mirror.
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — records this harness gap and its effect on the 2026-10-23 verdict (`finish_reason=length` → not testable).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required for this intake — the seed description (a `discovered-from` follow-up) fully specifies the desired capture, aggregation keys and rendering, and the residual decisions were resolvable by repo inspection. Decisions taken (recorded as assumptions above), with evidence:

- **Q (self-answered): Is a streaming capture path needed?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence): No. `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py:1071` sets `"stream": False` and builds the result from `resp.json()`; there is no streaming code path in this harness. Capture point is `choices[0].finish_reason`. Source: file inspection.
- **Q (self-answered): Which summary key name?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence): `finish_reason_counts`, matching `scripts/slot_history_extract.py:386/560/768` (`finish_reason_counts` + "Stream finish reasons" rendering). Source: file inspection.
- **Q (self-answered): How is a missing reason represented?** — Answer (agent, convention): explicitly counted (absent ≠ fabricated default), matching the module's existing "absent metrics are reported explicitly" convention (`ContentionMetrics.unavailable`). Source: `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` contention-metrics section.
- **Q (self-answered): Are historical runs backfilled or the reevaluation doc updated?** — Answer (agent): No. `restart_services()` clears the proxy log, so the 2026-10-23 metric is unrecoverable; the reevaluation doc is a historical record that already links this item (`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md:232,289,365`).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise
  for. Keep the gate.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before
  micro-tuning batch sizes, since the two interact.

## Plan (2026-10-25)

Decomposed into nine children. Every change-making child is dependency-blocked
on the **gate child** (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ, *Verify sustained local utilisation gate*) and on the gated geometry experiment
(LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), so nothing starts before AC0 is satisfied. This item
itself depends on the gate child and therefore renders as `blocked`.

| # | Child | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify sustained local utilisation gate (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ) | AC0 | — |
| 2 | Baseline prefill measurement capture (LP-0MVNBJWRH006V9Y6) | AC1 | 1 |
| 3 | 40-80k prefill benchmark capability (LP-0MVNBJX3G008IBTB) | AC2 (measurement validity) | 1, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 4 | Measurement evidence and log-consumer audit (LP-0MVNBJXF9002DJAZ) | AC5 | 1, 2 |
| 5 | Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD) | AC2 | 1, 2, 3, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 6 | Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints (LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51) | AC2 | 1, 5 |
| 7 | ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review (LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J) | AC2 (proxy knobs), AC4 | 1, 2, 5, 6 |
| 8 | Post-change verification: latency and stability (LP-0MVNBJYPM004UV56) | AC3, AC7 | 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 |
| 9 | Document launch flags and reproducibility (LP-0MVNBJZ100020UN0) | AC6 | 1, 5, 6 |

Sequence: gate -> baseline + harness capability (test-first) -> launch-flag
A/B -> guard review -> post-change verification + docs. Each child is a
vertical slice carrying its own tests, config/docs change and measurement
record.

Vertical-slice decision: the change is deliberately **not** phased into
separate "code" and "docs" phases; each A/B child lands flag + test + comment
together, because an undocumented or untested flag change is not deliverable.

**Effort/risk (this plan):** Medium (`recommended 51.22 h`, range 33.3-76.0 h)
/ **Medium** (score 10). Estimate source: `effort-and-risk` skill with this
plan's per-child WBS; it replaces the `0.00 h` autoplan placeholder recorded
earlier.

**Gate status at planning time:** NOT met (busy 2.2 % for the night
2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00; 10.2 % over the 24 h daily report).
Children that change configuration must not start until AC0 is satisfied.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Answered by repository / work-item evidence (non-interactive planning run):

- Q: "Is the AC0 gate (>60 % local busy for a full night) met?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`):
  **No.** 2.2 % busy for 2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00 (719 s of
  32 400 s, 27 streams, prefill 336 slot-s, decode 383 slot-s); 10.2 % for the
  24 h window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52. Source: CLI run recorded in
  the pre-check comment (`/tmp/wl-gate-check`).
- Q: "Has micro-batch tuning already been attempted, and with what result?"
  - Answer (evidence: LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`):
  yes - ubatch 1024 -> 2048 gave 1.04x at p90 over 20k+ batches and was
  reverted; the close-out rule is to re-measure at 40-80k tokens. The plan
  therefore spends one child on the 40-80k measurement capability first.
- Q: "Are the prefill-related proxy knobs still available to tune?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` + LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D): no - budget
  25 000 tokens, deadline 120 s, p75 pricing from 20k tokens and safety
  fraction 0.95 are already live. The plan re-validates their pricing after
  the launch-flag change instead of re-tuning them blind.

Open questions for the producer:

- **OPEN QUESTION** (geometry authority, directed to the producer): should the
  geometry prerequisite be LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN (*1 slot @262K vs 2 slots
  @131K*) - the experiment this item names - or LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5
  (*snapshot pool 2 -> 4 instead of more live slots*)? It matters because the
  winning geometry bounds the largest prompt the 40-80k harness can send and
  changes the micro-batch interaction. **Recommended:** keep
  LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN authoritative and treat LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5 as a
  parallel, independently decided item.
- **OPEN QUESTION** (gate window definition, directed to the producer): is
  "a full night" the wall-clock night used here (22:00-07:00) or the configured
  cheap window (01:00-10:00, `server.priority_window`)? **Recommended:**
  22:00-07:00, as written in AC0, with the busy % taken from the
  `definition: dispatch_to_finish` upper bound.

Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 04:20 UTC - plan session: pre-check deviation recorded, gate
  evidence captured (NOT met), duplicate-work check against 5 keywords, 9
  children created in test-first order, 20 dependency edges wired (all children
  gated on LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ; batch work additionally gated on LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), effort/risk
  re-estimated (Medium/Medium, 51.22 h recommended), six review stages run, AC
  coverage verified.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be

## Context

- Per-slot ctx is `--ctx-size / --parallel`: `--parallel 1 --ctx-size 262144` -> 262,144 per slot. `--parallel` and `session_slot_pool_size` MUST match or sessions map to nonexistent slots.
- The warm ceiling is `min(clamp, economic)` with economic = `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio x local_model_ctx_size)` (0.4578 x 262,144 ~= 120,049) and clamp = 258,048 at 1 slot. - The cold/warm band must keep non-zero width or the cached_ratio routing check stays unreachable (LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` becomes moot with one slot (prefill serialisation is inherent); record whether it is left as-is.

## Problem

`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489` carries a `# noqa` comment whose text is prose
rather than a comma-separated code list, so ruff cannot parse it as a
suppression. Every `ruff check` run in this repo — repo-wide or file-scoped —
prints a warning to stderr:

```
$ ruff check --select I001 proxy/proxy/handlers.py
warning: Invalid `# noqa` directive on proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489: expected a
comma-separated list of codes (e.g. `# noqa: F401, F841`).
All checks passed!
```

Current source:

```python
    import os  # noqa: local import for config access
```

## Why it matters

# slots_500_triage.py: progress-dot artifact causes child 503 lines to report as unknown

## Problem

`scripts/slots_500_triage.py`'s `_ACCESS_RE` regex fails to match `GET /slots` access lines that are physically prefixed with the tail of a llama-server progress-dot line (no newline between dots and the access line). Example:

```text
[60965] .......................srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 503
```

The regex expects `\s*` after the optional `[pid]` but encounters `.` characters instead, so the line is reported as `unknown:?` rather than being attributed to child `60965:503`. The live corpus contains **9** such lines versus **17** correctly attributed child 503s — a ~35% undercount of child-503 events.

## Users

- SRE/on-call engineers running the triage tool during incident response (F3 workflow).
- Automated audits (e.g. LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12) that depend on accurate responder splits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Regex tolerates leading dots.** `_ACCESS_RE` matches lines where `.` characters appear between the optional `[pid]` bracket and the `srv` keyword (e.g. `[.\s]*` instead of `\s*`). Verified against the example: `[60965] .......................srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 503` → matches with `pid=60965`, `status=503`.
- **AC2 — No regression on clean lines.** All existing corpus lines and the F3/incident fixtures (including `llama-server.log-2026-08-27.gz`) produce identical responder splits and counter values — no change to reported numbers.
- **AC3 — Tests.** `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` includes a test case driving a log fixture with progress-dot-prefixed 503 lines and asserts correct pid attribution (not `unknown`).
- **AC4 — Live corpus verification.** Running the triage tool on the live corpus now attributes all 9 previously-unparsed child-503 lines, bringing the child-503 count to the full 26.

## Constraints

- Do not change the responder classification logic (`router` = no `[pid]`, otherwise child pid).
- The fix is limited to `_ACCESS_RE` only — no other regexes or parsing logic.
- The dot artifact only appears on 503 lines in the current corpus, so the risk to other status codes is nil.

## Existing state

- `_ACCESS_RE` at `scripts/slots_500_triage.py:49` uses `\s*` between the optional `[pid]` and `srv`.
- Parent item LP-0MVVWTWGY004BO5H deliberately left `_ACCESS_RE` unchanged to keep that fix surgical.

## Desired change

Replace `\s*` with `[.\s]*` (or equivalent) in the `_ACCESS_RE` pattern to tolerate leading dot characters before `srv`.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — `_ACCESS_RE` definition (~line 49)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` — extend with dot-prefixed fixture test
- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — `analyze_slots_500` responder split (~line 112)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVVWTWGY004BO5H** — *slots_500_triage.py crashes on any /slots 503 response* — parent: fixes the KeyError crash; deliberately does not touch `_ACCESS_RE`.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — Epic parent covering the router-responder 400/500 verification work.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The regex change could match unintended lines if dots appear in other contexts. **Mitigation:** Only 503 lines in the corpus carry this artifact; the pattern `[.\s]*` is narrow enough to not cause false matches elsewhere.
- **Assumption:** The dot artifact is caused by llama-server's in-place progress-dot output not being flushed with a newline before the access log line; this is a known llama-server behaviour (hybrid-arch checkpoint re-prefill).
- **Risk:** Low. This is a minor data-quality fix with a small, well-contained code change.

## Scope Creep

- Improving the llama-server log format or fixing the dot artifact at the source is out of scope for this work item.

# Goal

Stop the status endpoint from **blocking on a synchronous `/slots` fetch**. Today
`get_llama_local_status()` performs its own counts query (2 s budget) *and* its own detail query
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s budget) in series, even though the periodic refresher already queries
`/slots` every 1 s and stamps `_last_slot_details_at`. That duplication doubles upstream load and
couples poll latency — and therefore `slots_stale` — to llama-server's slowest path.

# Design (smallest end-to-end slice)

- One shared snapshot provider: a single `/slots` fetch path produces `(counts, per-slot detail,
  fetched_at)`; counts and detail are derived from **the same payload**, so they can never disagree.
- The status handler serves that snapshot; it performs at most one bounded fresh fetch per poll and
  only when the snapshot is missing or older than the freshness budget.
- The refresher keeps a bounded timeout; a slow backend degrades to the previous snapshot instead of
  extending the poll.
- All existing payload contracts hold: `slots` annotation (`lease_state`, `phase`, ETA), the
  empty-array fallback, `capacity_hint` reconciliation, `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A status poll causes at most one upstream `/slots` fetch and reuses the shared snapshot when
  it is within the freshness budget (asserted by exact call count in tests).
- AC2: Handler wall-clock latency stays within budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` + 250 ms slack) when
  the backend hangs, verified by the hang-injection test.
- AC3: `available_slots`/`total_slots` and the per-slot `is_processing` values are always derived
  from one payload — a single-source test proves they cannot disagree.
- AC4: Payload parity: `slots`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`, annotation fields and
  `capacity_hint` are unchanged for consumers on equivalent backend data (parity test).
- AC5: Failure paths stay well-formed: empty snapshot ⇒ `slots: []`; snapshot older than
  `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` ⇒ counts fail closed (never served as current capacity).

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

# Reuse

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` already provides TTL caching plus single-flight (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` already carry a stamped snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` already keeps the cache pristine against log-derived data.

## Delivered baseline (2026-11-05) — read before starting

The read path still serialises its own two fetches, so this item's deliverable is unchanged:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py:846` awaits `_query_slots(...)` (counts) and `:893` awaits
  `_query_slots_detail(...)` (detail) one after the other before publishing.
- `slots_upstream_calls` is published per poll and the current comment states 0-or-1 "today" via
  single-flight/TTL coalescing — measure it rather than assume it; a poll must never fan out twice.

Reuse what has landed since this plan was written (do **not** add parallel machinery):

- `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` (`LOCAL_SLOTS_MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_SECONDS`; config-first) is
  the existing snapshot-age ceiling (LP-0MW1VVKPF001ZAV5). Past it the payload withholds slots and
  reports `slots_stale_reason="snapshot_too_old"`.
- `slots_stale_reason` is the canonical staleness vocabulary (LP-0MW1VVIPG008896N); `slots_stale`
  stays `counts_stale or detail_stale` until F4 decides otherwise, so this item must not change that
  semantic (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1281`).
- `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` / `slots_snapshot_source` are already published by F1 — extend them,
  do not rename them.

# Goal

Make `slots_stale` **measure staleness**, not cache use. Once the poll path serves a warm snapshot
by design, "served from cache" is true for almost every poll and the metric stops meaning anything.
Define freshness by the age of the snapshot the poll was served from, publish that age, and derive
`slots_stale` from it.

# Design

- Freshness budget: **reuse the delivered ceiling** `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`
  (`LOCAL_SLOTS_MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_SECONDS`, config-first, default ≈300 s — LP-0MW1VVKPF001ZAV5).
  It is already published as `slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`; do **not** introduce a second knob
  and do **not** resurrect the name `SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (it does not exist in code).
- `slot_snapshot_age_seconds` and `slots_snapshot_source` are **already published** (F1,
  `4d31d3ab`). `status_schema_version` is **7**, not 5 — schema 5 was superseded by
  LP-0MV1VVIPG008896N (6) and LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M (7). Any new field this item adds bumps to the
  next version; it must not renumber to 5.
- `slots_stale` today is `counts_stale or detail_stale` (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1281`), plus a
  forced `true` for `router_model_missing`. This item changes that derivation to
  `slot_snapshot_age_seconds > slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` (including the missing-snapshot
  case). `slots_detail_stale` keeps its current meaning for `capacity_hint` reconciliation;
  `slot_counts_stale` keeps its meaning for the counts fallback; `slots_stale_reason` keeps its
  precedence (`snapshot_too_old` dominates).
- Snapshot age is stamped from the **successful fetch** time on a monotonic clock, never from the
  poll's read time (the LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1 lesson: never re-stamp stale data as fresh).
- The analysis surfaces (`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`, nightly report producer) read
  the new fields.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `slots_stale=true` if and only if the served snapshot age exceeds
  `slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` (the delivered ceiling); the age is published in the payload and
  on the `status_request` line (table-driven test: `< budget`, `== budget`, `> budget`, no
  snapshot).
- AC2: The payload change is additive at whatever `status_schema_version` is current when this
  lands (7 at the time of writing) — a consumer ignoring the new behaviour observes unchanged
  fields, and the version bump this item makes (if any) is asserted by the contract test. Renumbering
  back to 5 is explicitly out of bounds.
- AC3: Snapshot age is monotonic-clock derived from the successful fetch, never negative, never
  reset by a cache read (a frozen-backend fixture must show the age growing monotonically).
- AC4: `capacity_hint` reconciliation still keys on `slots_detail_stale` and still yields no
  `saturated` while `local_in_flight_requests == 0` — all existing reconciliation tests pass
  unchanged.
- AC5: `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` reports `slots_stale` from the new definition and
  tolerates old-schema windows (pre-change lines without the age field are counted as before), with
  tests.
- AC6: The freshness-semantics decision is recorded on the parent with producer confirmation via
  `wl reviewed`, or the implementer records the explicit acceptance of the plan's recommended option
  (Appendix Q1) before coding.

# Key Files:

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`

# Reuse

- `_last_slot_details_at` already stamps the last successful fetch.
- `_latency_band` / attribution output in the analysis tool accepts additive fields.

## Freshness-semantics decision (producer, 2026-11-02) — AC6 record

The producer confirmed the plan's recommendation (**option A**, plan Q1 / producer question Q-D):

- `slots_stale = true` **iff** the age of the snapshot the poll was served from exceeds
  `SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (default `2.0` s, env-configurable).
- The payload publishes the age and provenance (`slot_snapshot_age_seconds`,
  `slots_snapshot_source`) and `status_schema_version` becomes `5` (additive).
- The metric is **not** redefined as "served from cache": after the shared-snapshot read path lands
  that condition holds for almost every poll and no longer measures staleness.
- Consumer note to carry into the docs: with the field name unchanged, rates measured before and
  after this change are not directly comparable — judge the `slots_stale < 5 %` target on
  post-change windows only (the old-schema tolerance in AC5 keeps historical windows readable).

This satisfies AC6's decision record; the confirmation is also recorded on the parent
(LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY, `## Producer decisions (2026-11-02)`), where `needsProducerReview` was cleared.
The item stays ordered behind F3 (producer decision Q-B = strict order).

## Correction (2026-11-05) — the 2026-11-02 decision record references a superseded payload

The record above was written when schema 5 was the next free version. It is not any more, and the
ceiling it calls for has since shipped under a different name. What changed:

| 2026-11-02 record | Delivered reality (2026-11-05) |
|---|---|
| `SLOTS_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (default `2.0` s) | `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` / `LOCAL_SLOTS_MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_SECONDS`, config-first, default ≈300 s (LP-0MW1VVKPF001ZAV5) |
| `status_schema_version` becomes `5` | already **7** (6 = `slots_stale_reason`, 7 = availability/detail truth) |
| payload gains `slot_snapshot_age_seconds` / `slots_snapshot_source` | already published by F1 |
| `slots_stale` becomes age-derived | **not done** — still `counts_stale or detail_stale` |

So the producer's intent (measure real staleness by snapshot age, publish the age and the reason)
is already half-delivered; the remaining gap is the `slots_stale` **derivation** itself.

### DECISION (producer, 2026-11-05) — AC6 record: **option A**, `slots_stale` becomes age-derived

The producer chose **option A**, answering the narrowed question above. This item is therefore
**not** descoped to a regression fence: it implements the derivation change on top of the delivered
baseline. The earlier 2026-11-02 decision (also option A) stands in intent; only the mechanics below
are updated to the delivered code.

Binding contract for this item:

- `slots_stale = true` **iff** `slot_snapshot_age_seconds > slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`
  (missing snapshot ⇒ `true`). The current union `counts_stale or detail_stale`
  (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1281`) is **replaced**, not supplemented.
- `slots_stale_reason` keeps its vocabulary and precedence (`snapshot_too_old` dominates). A fresh
  snapshot inside the ceiling must yield `slots_stale=false` **and** `slots_stale_reason=null` even
  when the detail phase served a cache entry — that is the exact behaviour this decision changes.
- `slots_detail_stale`, `slot_counts_stale`, `slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`,
  `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` and `slots_snapshot_source` keep their current names and meanings.
  **No renames and no second freshness knob.**
- The forced `true` for `router_model_missing` is retained: the proxy holds no live evidence at all
  in that state, so the surface can never be treated as inside the ceiling.
- `capacity_hint` reconciliation keeps keying on `slots_detail_stale`, so AC4 is unaffected by the
  derivation change.
- **Comparability:** the field name is unchanged but its meaning tightens, so pre- and post-change
  rates are not comparable. The `< 5 %` parent target is judged on **post-change windows only**;
  carried into F6 (LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP) which produces the AC2 verdict.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the ETA-ordering starvation bound to be a value that can
actually fire under the shipped wait budget, so a long prefill that keeps losing
the queue is still promotable (or the knob is retired as inert).

## Discovery

Found while sweeping the queue caps to 30 s / depth 2
(`LP-0MVT1146V007WXA4`). `proxy/config.yaml` ships
`contention_queue_eta_promotion_seconds: 30` and, after the sweep,
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30`. The promotion bound only takes effect
for a waiter already past 30 s in the queue, but the wait budget expires it at
exactly 30 s — so promotion can never fire and
`contention_queue_eta_ordering` loses its starvation guard.

Not fixed there because the item's AC7 scopes the sweep to the two cap values
("no behavioural change beyond the two config values"); this is a follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Decide (recorded on the item) between: (a) lowering
   `contention_queue_eta_promotion_seconds` to a value strictly below the
   shipped wait budget, or (b) retiring the knob as inert and documenting that
   depth 2 limits reorder scope enough that starvation cannot occur.
2. Whichever is chosen, a test pins the invariant
   `contention_queue_eta_promotion_seconds < contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`
   for the shipped config (or asserts the knob is documented as retired), so a
   future budget/depth change cannot silently make promotion inert again.
3. `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/docs/routing.md` state the resulting
   relationship between the promotion bound and the wait budget.

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want one INFO log line per compaction-header emission
(and one distinguishable line when compaction was evaluated but emitted
nothing), so that reading the proxy log tells me whether the signal was
emitted at all — closing secondary finding 2 of the parent ("Header emission
logs nothing ... a loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken
one") and satisfying AC4's proxy half.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — this is required whether or not
Phase A/B pass.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py:397` `_build_compaction_headers()` returns `{}` or the
  header dict; the only log statement in it is
  `logger.debug("Failed to build compaction headers; omitting", ...)` on the
  exception path (`router.py:430`). The success path logs nothing.
- `router.py:2336` applies it with `outgoing_headers.update(...)` on the
  streaming path; a second site near `router.py:3551` covers the buffered path.
- `router_helpers.py:6218` already logs `session_compaction applied
  session=… priority=… est_before=… est_after=…` — but that line proves
  *compaction happened*, not that *headers were emitted*. The two can diverge
  (e.g. `compaction_summary_text` empty → no headers, compaction still
  applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: On the live-applied path, exactly one INFO line per response is logged:
  `compaction_headers emitted session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`. It is logged once per response on
  both the streaming (SSE) and buffered response paths — never once per SSE
  chunk.
- AC2: A response that evaluated compaction but emitted no headers logs exactly
  one line naming the reason, distinguishable from "emitted": one of
  `compaction_headers none reason=disabled|below_trigger|noop|dry_run|
  remote_with_guidance|no_summary_text|build_failed`. `no_summary_text` covers
  the real divergence case (compaction applied, summary missing) and
  `build_failed` covers the exception path.
- AC3: No header-emission line is emitted for requests that never reach the
  compaction path (e.g. remote dispatch with no session), keeping router log
  volume unchanged for the overwhelmingly common `compaction_disabled` case at
  a rate that permits long-window analysis (the `session_compaction applied`
  line already fires per compacted request; the new line must not multiply
  log volume for non-compaction traffic).
- AC4: The fail-safe contract is unchanged and better observed: an exception
  while building headers still yields no headers and never changes dispatch,
  but is now logged at **WARNING** with `exc_info=True` (was `debug`), so a
  silently broken emission is visible in normal operation.
- AC5: Header names, values and encodings are untouched:
  `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` passes **unmodified**.
- AC6: Unit tests assert: the AC1 line and each field on both response paths;
  exactly one AC1 line per response with a multi-chunk SSE stream; the AC2
  reason line for `disabled` / `below_trigger` / `dry_run` /
  `remote_with_guidance` / `no_summary_text`; WARNING + `exc_info` on the
  exception path; and that a logging failure cannot raise out of the emission
  path (fail-safe preserved).
- AC7: No marker text, no summary body and no message content appear in any
  log line — only ids, counts and lengths.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Goal

**Conditional.** If Phase A or Phase B fails because the client's rebuilt base
is not recognised as the proxy's base, implement base identity so the
divergence is detected explicitly (with a base id) instead of degrading
silently into `history_mismatch` and a from-scratch re-summarisation.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8, Phase C + AC5. **Do not implement speculatively**
— this child exists so the repair is scoped and ready, and must be closed as
"not needed" when both T1 and T2 pass.

## Gate (must be checked before any code)

- If `Phase A verdict: PASS` **and** `Phase B verdict: PASS` → close this child
  with `--reason "Not needed: Phase A and Phase B both PASS (<verdict links>);
  AC5 remains unmet by design because no divergence was observed"` and change
  no code.
- Otherwise implement exactly the failing link. Phase A fail ⇒ the producer
  contract is the defect (no base id is meaningful yet; fix the link named on
  the T1 child and re-run T1 instead of building the handshake). Phase B fail
  with a recorded fail signature ⇒ implement the handshake below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The proxy emits `X-Compaction-Base-Id` with the compaction header set:
  a stable hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex chars) of the **exact** compacted message
  list it dispatched; the same list always yields the same id and any change to
  roles, order or content changes it. The hash input/serialisation is
  documented in a docstring so the client can reproduce it.
- AC2: The proxy accepts `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` on the request. On a match it
  adopts the client's base instead of re-summarising (no CREATION
  re-summarisation) and logs
  `compaction_base adopt session=<id8> base=<id8>` at INFO.
- AC3: On a mismatch the proxy logs one WARNING naming both ids
  (`compaction_base mismatch session=<id8> proxy_base=<id8>
  client_base=<id8>`), re-signals once (emits the header set again on that
  response), and does **not** report `history_mismatch` for this cause.
- AC4: A second consecutive divergence for the same session stops mirroring for
  that session and logs the reason at WARNING
  (`compaction_base mirroring_off session=<id8> reason=second_divergence`);
  subsequent responses for that session carry no `X-Compaction-*` headers, so
  the client cannot loop.
- AC5: Clients that send no `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` behave exactly as today
  (contract preserved; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` green
  unmodified) — the handshake is additive and opt-in on the client side.
- AC6: No payload content, marker text or summary body appears in any log line
  or header beyond the existing base64 marker — only ids and counts.
- AC7: Unit tests cover: hash determinism and sensitivity (reordered turns,
  changed content, changed role); adopt-on-match (no summariser call — asserted
  with a summariser spy); single-mismatch re-signal (exactly one extra emission);
  second-divergence mirroring-off; absent-client-header passthrough; and that a
  malformed/truncated base id is treated as absent, not as a mismatch.
- AC8: The bridge (SorraAgents) sends `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` when it has captured
  a signal, and clears it when it clears state; its unit tests extend to cover
  send/clear. Recorded with the SorraAgents commit hash on this item.
- (Parent AC5) if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.

- Producer: compute the base id once, where the compacted list is built
  (`router_helpers.py` live-applied path), carry it on the session result
  alongside `compaction_summary_text`, and add it to
  `_build_compaction_headers`. Mismatch handling lives where the session store
  is compared (`session_manager.py` / `session.py`), reusing the existing
  `fallback_reason` plumbing rather than adding a second path.
- Client: reuse the existing per-session state map — store the id with the
  signal, add it to the outgoing header set in the dispatch path; no new
  persistence.
- Keep the "re-signal exactly once" counter in the existing per-session store,
  not in a new global.

## Deliverables

- Bridge dispatch-header plumbing + tests.
- A paragraph in `docs/session-compaction-design.md` §7.3 describing the
  handshake and its stop condition.

## Goal

Decide deliberately whether the second local slot is capacity or waste, and make the system use it (or stop advertising it as available).

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- llama-server runs 2 slots (total_slots=2, n_ctx 131072 each) and session_slot_pool_size is 2, but from task 191941 (08:43) through roughly task 193700 every launch was slot id 0 -- about 1,200 consecutive tasks on one slot. Slot 1 reappeared at task 193715 only once two requests genuinely overlapped.
- Normal agent traffic is not slot-pinned: id_slot is set only by compaction_summarizer.py; mainline requests let llama-server choose, and it picks by prompt-prefix similarity (1,040 selected slot by LCP similarity versus 39 by LRU). With the proxy granting one dispatch lease at a time there is never a second in-flight request, so slot 0 always wins and slot 1 is never launched.
- The signals disagree: available_slots reported 0 (lease-derived) at 08:50:47 while llama had a free slot, and 2 at 08:49:31 while the lease gate denied a dispatch.

- AC1: Root cause recorded with supporting log evidence for why slot 1 goes unused in serialised operation, including the LCP-similarity versus LRU selection behaviour.

- AC3: The chosen option is implemented behind tests: a two-concurrent-session test asserts either two slots are used with reused prefixes, or the second request waits with an accurate capacity signal.

# Launch authority: detect a foreign backend and refuse to spawn

**Parent:** LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 · **Type:** feature · **Phase 2 of 8**

## Context

`_try_adopt_running_llama_server()` decides ownership from
`proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` alone, and `start_llama_server()` spawns
unconditionally. When a container started outside the lifecycle holds port 8080
the proxy therefore adopts a server it did not start, then spawns doomed
host-side processes against the busy port (six `<defunct> llama-server` entries
on 2026-11-04).

## Change

Introduce a single authority check that inspects the **live** listener before
any adopt-or-spawn decision:

- New module `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` exposing
  `inspect_running_backend(srv) -> BackendInspection` with fields
  `present`, `pids`, `container` (name or `None`), `parallel`, `slot_save_path`,
  `lifecycle_owned`, `source` (`"absent" | "lifecycle" | "foreign"`).
- Reuse the existing, already container-aware helpers rather than duplicating
  them: `proxy.backend_rss.discover_llama_pids`, `_cmdline`,
  `container_name`, `container_init_pid`, and `lifecycle._find_pid_on_port`.
  Read the effective flags from the process `cmdline` (works for host and
  container: the container shares the host pid namespace).
- Wire the check into `_startup_launch_default_model_loader()` (and the
  on-demand `ensure_model_loaded()` spawn path) *before* adoption or spawn.
- On `source == "foreign"`: log one ERROR naming port, pid/container, resolved
  slot count and live `--parallel`, set a sticky `local_backend_foreign` flag,
  refuse local dispatch, and return without calling
  `subprocess.Popen`/`podman` — never leave defunct children.
- Surface the verdict in `/health` (`llama_backend_source`,
  `llama_backend_container`) and `/llama/local/status`.

## Policy decision (confirmed by the producer, 2026-11-05)

**Refuse and report.** A backend the lifecycle did not start is never adopted
and never taken over: the proxy refuses to spawn, reports the mismatch (port,
pid/container, resolved slot count, live `--parallel`) and leaves the running
process untouched, so an operator decides what to do with it. Taking ownership
is explicitly out of scope — stopping a working backend on a detection error is
a worse failure than reporting it.

Ownership is proven by (a) the tracked `llama_process` handle this proxy
spawned, or (b) a matching recorded signature **plus** a live process whose
`--parallel` and launch flags agree with the config. A signature match alone is
no longer sufficient — that is the gap this item closes. The proxy keeps
serving remote providers; the local tier fails closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Startup detects a llama-server the lifecycle did not start (host or container) and reports it explicitly, including the port, pid/container and the resolved slot count.
- [ ] No defunct host-side `llama-server` processes are produced when a container holds the port (test drives the lifecycle with the port pre-occupied).
- [ ] A signature match alone never yields `lifecycle_owned`; the live process flags must also agree.
- [ ] `/health` and `/llama/local/status` expose the backend source and, for a container holder, its name.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `inspect_running_backend()`: discover pids → read `cmdline` → parse
   `--parallel`/`-np` and `--slot-save-path` → resolve container via
   `backend_rss.container_name` → classify ownership.
2. Guard both spawn call sites with the inspection result.
3. Extend the health/status payload builders (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`).
4. Document the behaviour in `docs/dev/proxy-log-lifecycle.md` (lifecycle
   section) or a new `docs/dev/llama-launch-authority.md`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/launch_authority.py` (new)
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`
- `proxy/proxy/backend_rss.py` (reuse, no behaviour change)
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `docs/dev/llama-launch-authority.md` (new)

## Dependencies

Blocked by the test item (Phase 1) so the red baseline exists first.
